A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AWM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-lineage experiments on 60 positive and 90 negative model pairs, including comparisons with HuRef and REEF.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and reports additional baseline results, vocabulary-overlap and CKA ablations, and explicit weight-manipulation tests.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains shared-vocabulary embedding alignment through LAP, permutation/sign recovery, and aggregation of unbiased CKA similarities for Q/K weights. Appendix H elaborates existing choices, including layer matching; the CKA alternatives are ablations, not changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds explicit permutation, sign-flip, constant-scaling and orthogonal-transformation test scenarios across five existing model families. The original model collection and six post-training categories remain unchanged; the newly listed training corpora document existing models rather than expand coverage.

E2.justification: Section 6.4 and Table 3 add PCS, identified as another HuRef measure, and Intrinsic Fingerprint as evaluated comparators. HuRef, now clarified as ICS, and REEF remain. This substantially broadens the principal comparison, although Figures 1–2 and Table 2 retain their original comparator sets.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols vary shared-token counts from 10 to 10,000, compare linear/RBF kernels with biased/unbiased CKA, and apply four transformations to five models. The original 150-pair evaluation and its metrics are retained; no revision of its existing settings is established.

E4.justification: V2 introduces systematic vocabulary-overlap sensitivity analysis in Figure 3, kernel/estimator ablations in Table 4, and explicit manipulation-robustness tests in Table 6. These directly investigate alignment requirements, CKA design choices and transformation invariance, questions without corresponding empirical analyses in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same negative-pair-based Z-score reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional averages and CKA comparisons do not introduce uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds Intrinsic Fingerprint and PCS results, including overall AUCs of 0.957 and 0.860. Figure 3 and Table 4 add sensitivity and CKA-variant outcomes; Table 6 reports 100% similarity in every model–manipulation cell. Existing AWM, HuRef and REEF results remain unchanged, so these are added findings rather than improved same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Equation 6 replaces the RMSNorm expression involving XX^T 1_m with the per-row squared-sum expression (X ⊙ X)1_n. Appendix E.3 updates the corresponding derivation and explicitly states row-norm invariance under orthogonal transformations. This is a localized mathematical correction; the theorem statements and remaining theory are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: training-free weight fingerprinting, robustness across six post-training categories, perfect classification on the 150-pair testbed, and computation within 30 seconds on an NVIDIA 3090. Additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets the method as requiring little vocabulary overlap and argues that unbiased estimation is important. It also explains retaining the linear kernel for efficiency despite stronger RBF separation. Appendix I connects its manipulation results to the theoretical analysis; the main interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The expanded model table adds training-corpus descriptions and direct checkpoint links to previously listed models. V2 also adds a supplementary-code statement and consolidates implementation choices in Appendix H. The existing GitHub link remains; these are documentation and access-information additions, not evidence of implementation changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands fingerprinting coverage into white-box and black-box approaches, discussing static weights, activations, gradients, output distributions and trigger queries. Added works include DeepJudge, EasyDetector, TensorGuard and LLMmap, alongside a broader discussion of black-box robustness limitations.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites and subdivides the fingerprinting discussion, adds explanatory transitions in Section 4, and expands the appendix organization with disclosure, ablation and implementation sections. Affiliation/contact text changes and the acknowledgement is removed. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the six-panel Figure 3 and result Tables 4 and 6, expands Table 3 with two comparator blocks, and redesigns the original model-mapping table as Table 5 with a training-corpus column and checkpoint links. The existing ROC and heatmap figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important validation gaps by testing vocabulary dependence, CKA design choices and explicit weight manipulations, while broadening baseline comparisons. These additions substantially strengthen support for the retained method; the RMSNorm correction and checkpoint documentation also improve technical reliability and reproducibility. Manipulation settings remain sparse, and Table 4's linear/unbiased averages are not reconciled with Table 3, but these qualifications do not outweigh the added direct evidence.
